claims.text: The untreated high-entropy alloy has a relatively coarse, homogeneous microstructure without engineered coupling between grains and nanoprecipitates.
A nanohierarchical architecture with spatial composition undulation and nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates can be engineered in a multicomponent alloy.
The nanohierarchical, composition-undulated architecture activates adaptive friction-interface protection.
Adaptive friction-interface protection produced by this architecture significantly lowers coefficient of friction.
Adaptive friction-interface protection produced by this architecture significantly reduces wear.
The architecture provides ultralow wear from room temperature through 800 °C.
The proposed benefits remain effective under both low and high mechanical loading.
At lower temperatures, the nano-coupled structure releases gradient frictional stress in stages through multiple deformation pathways.
Lower-temperature gradient stress relief minimizes adhesive wear.
At elevated temperature, sliding activates a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
The high-temperature nanocrystalline glaze layer reduces oxidative wear.
The high-temperature nanocrystalline glaze layer reduces abrasive wear.
The architecture facilitates favorable microstructural evolution and tribo-reactions during sliding.
The engineered alloy should achieve wear rates on the order of 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm3/(N·m).
The engineered alloy should have a lower wear rate than an untreated alloy under matched loading and temperature conditions.
The engineered alloy should have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than an untreated alloy under matched conditions.
Untreated high-entropy alloys display higher friction coefficients and wear rates throughout the specified temperature range.
The benefit persists only while the nanohierarchical structure remains stable under mechanical and thermal stresses up to 800 °C.
The wear-protection strategy demonstrated in the Ni50(AlNbTiV)50-type system can be transferred broadly to other high-entropy-alloy systems.

contradictions.description: The boundary conditions exclude cases in which the nanohierarchical structure becomes unstable, whereas the falsification rule treats premature structural degradation as falsifying the hypothesis. Thus, degradation is simultaneously outside the claimed applicability domain and a decisive falsifier.
